items.title: Darfur: Healthcare needs outstrip resources as Security Council extends Sudan sanctions
items.summary: More than 700,000 displaced people in Tawila, in Sudan’s war-ravaged Darfur region, face severe shortages of healthcare, food, water and protection, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Thursday as it called for an urgent increase in resources.

items.title: Russian Strikes against Ukraine Have Reached ‘New Horrifying Level’, Top United Nations Peacebuilding Official Warns Security Council, amid Calls for Immediate Ceasefire
items.summary: Russian Federation strikes have killed over 100 civilians across Ukraine this week, United Nations officials told the Security Council today, warning that intensifying attacks on cities and critical infrastructure threaten to leave millions without electricity, heating and water as winter approaches.

items.title: World News in Brief: ‘Horrific’ attack in Sudan, Israeli incursions in Syria intensify, most women and girls homeless in Gaza
items.summary: A suspected drone strike has left at least 40 dead in Sudan’s Blue Nile State – near the Ethiopian border - according to initial reports from the ground, according to UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric. Most of the casualties were women and girls.

items.title: Security Council LIVE: Yemen has fallen back into full-scale war, warns UN envoy
items.summary: The Security Council met to discuss the crisis in Yemen Friday, where a Houthi offensive launched in September has sharply escalated the 12-year-long war for control of the country and spillover from the US-Iran war has provoked a new displacement crisis. Live coverage below and for full meetings updates, go here.

items.title: Yemen Has Returned to Full-Scale War, Threatening Regional Stability, Top UN Officials Warn Security Council, Urging Dialogue, Unfettered Humanitarian Access
items.summary: As fighting intensifies across Yemen and attacks on civilian infrastructure threaten regional stability and vital Red Sea shipping routes, senior United Nations officials briefing the Security Council today called for an end to hostilities, unhindered humanitarian access and a return to negotiations.

items.title: Five Energy Market Factors That Could Tip the Scales in the Middle East War
items.summary: Oil, gas and fuel prices are central to the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, with Washington striving to lower them and Tehran to keep them high. With both sides determined to prevail, five market-shaping developments in particular could affect whether fighting ramps up or de-escalates.

items.summary: Six weeks after Nepal’s deadly flooding disaster, communities are still struggling to rebuild their lives, but they will need sustained help as global warming increases the risk of another Himalayan catastrophe, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Friday.

items.summary: The aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln returned to its home port of San Diego after 321 days during which it spearheaded the Navy's involvement in Operation Epic Fury and enforced a maritime blockade against Iranian-flagged vessels in the northern Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman.

items.title: Daily Press Briefing by the Office of the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General
items.summary: The International Organization for Migration said today that nearly all of Gaza’s population, almost 2 million human beings, still require shelter assistance one year after a ceasefire was announced. Over half of all tents and makeshift shelters currently in use are in poor condition and require replacement.
